notes: All 240 Sofa IDs S000-S239 were inspected across sofa_01.jpg through sofa_08.jpg. Full-size originals were additionally inspected for the decisions marked true. This is assistant visual QA, not externally verified ground truth.
Quarantine retains the original annotations unchanged. It includes confirmed missing targets, class ambiguity and unresolved edge furniture. No automatic pseudo-labels were promoted to ground truth.

Manual groups conservatively join repeated objects, color/product variants, matching furniture sets and clearly repeated room/view series. Unique unrelated items use their own ID. Groups should be unioned with exact/perceptual groups before split allocation.
Repeated ornate sofa S123-S147 uses a wooden staircase banister on the right, which is not a chair. S130 separately shows a dark side table/stool and is quarantined.
S234/S235 were confirmed in full-size originals to show floor reflection and loose curtains below the sofa, not a second sofa. S229/S237 in the same series do include a foreground coffee table.
Plant pots, narrow plant holders, rugs, lamps, baskets, shelves, people and decorative objects alone were not treated as missing Chair/Sofa/Table annotations.

Potential cross-class room candidate: S224/S227/S236/S239 have white walls, glossy pale floor tiles and black skirting. Compare to the Chair reviewer family; no cross-class identity was independently confirmed by this reviewer.
Several single-seat versus loveseat distinctions (S152/S173/S178/S222) require a consistent class definition. They were conservatively quarantined rather than relabeled.

The outdoor metal-door scene group S105-S110 is conservative scene grouping for related furniture photographs; the tan flat-back product group joins highly similar design views, preventing product-family leakage.

The hand-picked conservative subset is intended as a first fine-tuning practice set; contact-sheet QA cannot prove exhaustive annotation correctness and does not replace later high-resolution annotation audit.
